sections.title: Featured projects
sections.lede: Selected work across generative AI, statistical modeling and machine learning. The name links to the code, Live opens the project, Writeup opens the long-form page on how it works and what it found.
projects: A live skill-assessment platform: Elo-style calibration recalibrated from real quiz responses, live peer percentiles, and three LLM-backed features (resume-gap analysis, a mock-interview agent, a personalized study guide). Full-stack, $0/month infrastructure.

An EV road-trip planner built around the battery a car actually has after five years: elevation- and weather-adjusted range modeling over live routing data, charger selection under a hard reserve constraint, and hazard-aware rerouting within a user-set detour budget.
An interactive Mandarin tutor built from any Chinese EPUB: pinyin over every character, natural read-aloud, and offline speak-back pronunciation grading.
Learn to speak Cantonese from today's HK news plus a 96-scenario everyday-conversations curriculum: LLM rewrite with a review pass, neural zh-HK audio, jyutping, tap-to-compare, and speech grading.
Drop in any EPUB and see its reading grade level, vocabulary richness, and word-coverage curve. Runs entirely in the browser, nothing uploaded.
Semantic search over 130k wine reviews using hybrid BM25 and dense retrieval with a cross-encoder reranker, evaluated on retrieval quality (precision and nDCG up roughly 21%).
A LangGraph agent that iteratively drafts and revises a training plan until it satisfies explicit safety checks, with a Streamlit interface.
Survival analysis (Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression) of how long track-and-field world records stand, estimating each record's probability of falling.
Distribution fitting and extreme-value theory locating any marathon time within a field of 31,842 finishers and quantifying how far the world record sits beyond it.

sections.title: Applied AI engineering
sections.lede: Four photo-to-structured-data apps pairing an LLM pipeline with a small model locally fine-tuned (LoRA) on the same task, each benchmarked base vs. fine-tuned vs. Claude zero-shot.
projects: Photograph a wine label for a grounded profile and food pairings cited to real reviews; a fine-tuned Qwen2.5-1.5B LoRA guesses grape variety from a blind tasting note alone, beating Claude's zero-shot Top-1 (27.7% vs. 23.0%).
Photograph a restaurant menu for cuisine and allergen-risk tags per dish; a fine-tuned LoRA reaches 99.3% cuisine accuracy and 69.3% allergen recall from a bare dish name.
Photograph a receipt for automatic spend-category tagging; a fine-tuned LoRA reaches 90.5% category accuracy on held-out merchants, versus 27.7% for the base model and 56.0% for zero-shot Claude.
Photograph a race course map for a verified km-by-km pacing plan checked against five deterministic rules; a fine-tuned Qwen2.5-3B LoRA reaches near-parity with Claude on structure and plausibility.

sections.title: Generative AI and agents
projects: Grounded retrieval-augmented Q&A that cites its sources, evaluated with an LLM-as-judge faithfulness metric; includes a LangChain LCEL implementation.
A LangGraph agent that infers a wine style and calls the retriever as a LangChain tool, with full run tracing.

sections.title: Running and sports analytics
projects: K-means clustering and PCA of 43 nations across five athletics disciplines, identifying five distinct performance archetypes.
Non-parametric hypothesis testing (Kruskal-Wallis) on 6,400 elite marks, assessing whether World Athletics points are comparable across events.
Regression of Boston Marathon field times on temperature: roughly one minute slower per degree F (r = 0.86).
Split analysis showing only 2.5% of 31,912 Boston finishers ran a faster second half.
Per-5K split analysis locating where marathon pace decays, around 30 km.
An equity analysis of Boston qualifying standards across age and gender brackets.
A three-framework comparison of finishing speed across the six World Marathon Majors.
Decomposition of recent marathon progression into footwear effects versus other factors.

sections.title: Language and NLP
projects: Fifty years of Billboard lyrics: longer and more repetitive over time, with roughly stable vocabulary.
A corpus study of lexical complexity in reality-television dialogue.

sections.title: Consumer and finance
projects: How 130k professional reviews cluster into an effective 8-point band on the nominal 100-point scale.
A Monte-Carlo retirement simulator estimating the probability a portfolio lasts through retirement.

sections.title: Apps and tools
projects: A routing tool that computes when to depart to arrive on time, using the Google Maps API.
A desktop app that converts e-books into read-along audiobooks (English and Chinese).
Converts an e-book or article into a two-host podcast with synthetic voices.
